- Purchase is inside the window at a listed retailer (T4), so no issue there.
- Destruction photo (T5) reportedly is a digital graphic rather than a physical product with marker writing, which would also require needs_info, but the deny from the label takes precedence.
- No duplicates (T6).

The first triggered rule in priority order is deny, based on the legible label showing a non-recalled model.

reasons.text: The label photo is legible and shows model AD10009GR, which is not a recalled model. Under the claim policy, a legible label showing a non-recalled model means the unit is not part of the recall, so the claim is denied even though the typed model AD10007GR is on the list.
The typed model AD10007GR matches the recall list, but the policy makes the label photo the controlling evidence, and the label reads a different, non-recalled model.
The purchase was at a listed retailer (Amazon.com) within the sale window, so purchase requirements are met; this does not offset the model denial.
No duplicate claims were found, so the denial is not affected by a duplicate review.
